title: Model Context Protocol
content:
Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard for connecting AI models to external tools, data sources, and systems in a structured, secure way.

Key points:
- Client-server architecture: an MCP client (e.g., an AI app) connects to one or more MCP servers, each exposing a set of capabilities.
- Core primitives: Tools (callable functions the model can invoke), Resources (data the model can read, like files or DB records), and Prompts (reusable prompt templates).
- Transport: communication typically happens over stdio (local) or HTTP/SSE (remote), using JSON-RPC messages.
- Discovery: clients can query a server to list its available tools/resources before using them, so the model only sees relevant, permitted capabilities.
- Safety: servers control exactly what's exposed and can enforce permissions, so the model interacts with external systems (databases, APIs, local files) without needing direct, unrestricted access.
- Common uses: connecting an AI assistant to Google Drive, Slack, GitHub, databases, or custom internal tools without writing one-off integrations for each.

In short: MCP standardizes how AI models discover and call external capabilities, similar to how a plugin system lets an app add new functionality without changing its core code.

title: TypeScript
content:
TypeScript is a modern version of JavaScript. It's a superset of JavaScript developed by Microsoft that adds static typing on top of JS. Key points:

- Any valid JavaScript is also valid TypeScript — you can adopt it gradually.
- You add type annotations (e.g. `let age: number = 30;`) so the compiler can catch type-related bugs before the code even runs, rather than at runtime.
- It compiles ("transpiles") down to plain JavaScript, so it runs anywhere JS runs (browsers, Node, etc.).
- It gives much better autocomplete, refactoring, and inline documentation in editors like VS Code, since the tooling knows the exact shape of your data.
- Popular in larger codebases and teams because it makes code easier to understand and safer to change.

title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
content: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard for connecting AI models to external tools, data sources, and systems in a structured, secure way. It defines a common interface so an AI assistant can discover available tools/resources from an "MCP server" and call them, rather than needing custom integration code for every service. This makes it easier to plug things like file systems, databases, or third-party apps into an AI workflow safely and consistently.
